summary.headline: Shyam Metalics Q1 FY27 revenue rose 23.3% YoY to INR5,455 crore and EBITDA rose 28.3% to INR812 crore, with margin at 14.9%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations reached INR5,455 crore, up 23.3% YoY and 4.1% QoQ, while EBITDA was INR812 crore (14.9% margin, up from 14.3% a year ago). Operating EBITDA was INR765 crore at a 14% margin and PAT was INR351 crore (6.4% margin), up 20.6% YoY. The company declared an interim dividend of INR1.8 per share and said the aluminium foil plant in Odisha has begun commissioning, with the aluminium flat roll project on track for Q2. Management also took a 26% stake in Emerge Green Power, a renewable energy vehicle, and shifted its solar strategy from capex to a JV-based model.

financial_highlights.change: vs 14.3% in Q1 FY26 and 14.4% in Q4 FY26
+20.6% YoY, +12.6% QoQ; margin vs 6% in prior quarter

segments.name: Aluminium
segments.commentary: Management attributed higher aluminium EBITDA per ton (up about 52% YoY per analyst) to LME prices and product mix. The Odisha aluminium foil plant has started commissioning; full operations expected to take 3-4 months, with real value expected from Q3.

segments.name: Flat products / colour-coated (CRM)
segments.commentary: Colour-coated plant commissioned in April 2026, lifting cold rolling capacity by 60% to 0.4 million tons. Management expects flat product numbers to more than double in FY27. CRM EBITDA was about INR8,500 per ton in the quarter, which management said may moderate.

segments.name: Stainless steel
segments.commentary: Current run rate of about INR130-140 crore revenue per quarter. Management expects INR600-700 crore once the new plant reaches 70-80% utilisation. Vision 2031 assumes about INR14,000 per ton EBITDA, with mix of roughly two-thirds 200/400 series and 35-40% 300 series.

segments.name: Specialty alloys
segments.commentary: Analyst computed Q1 FY27 specialty alloy EBITDA margin around 20.5%, versus the roughly 15% implied by the FY31 vision. Management said demand is strong and no major capacity expansion is declared, though it is under evaluation.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for 2031 EBITDA margin of about 14-15% (long-term aspiration) and 600-700 bps improvement in ROE and ROCE by 2031; also cited a 15-17% overall business margin in a later answer.

Management is guiding FY27 growth above 20% in terms of numbers, with EBITDA growth of more than 20-25%. Analyst math of 30-35% EBITDA growth was acknowledged as possibly conservative; the chairman said projections are more than 25%.
Remaining announced capex of about INR9,580 crore to be deployed over the next 3-4 years, primarily funded through internal accruals.
Iron-making facilities and power plants expected to be commissioned around end of Q2 / early Q3 FY27; Q3 and Q4 are described as important for value-added contribution.
Another downstream capex leg is under Board evaluation, with clarity expected by Q3.
Interim dividend of INR1.8 per share declared; INR4,500 crore fundraising approval described as an enabling resolution only.
capex_capacity: Colour-coated plant commissioned April 2026, cold rolling capacity up 60% to 0.4 million tons.
Aluminium foil facility in Odisha commissioning; aluminium flat roll project on track for Q2 FY27 commissioning.
HR coil plant to produce about 2 million tons; flat steel volume target of 1.7-1.8 million tons by 2031.
Specialty steel: auto steel plant and SBQ mill at Ramsarup, expected to be commissioned by end of next year.
Beneficiation plant commissioned to use low-grade iron ore.

Solar strategy shifted from capex to an opex/JV model, with 26% stake in Emerge Green Power Private Limited (a PE-backed venture fund, not a related party). Some power plants expected to be commissioned in Q2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management said Indian steel demand grows 7-8% a year and rebar accounts for about 50-55% of steel consumption; the recent rebar price fall was described as a seasonal monsoon effect.
Export business of about INR2,000 crore provides natural hedge; management said most raw materials are sourced domestically.
Management said the company is moving toward B2C and value-added products, with competition in CRM described as intense.

qa_highlights.question: Is aluminium EBITDA per ton up about 52% YoY driven by LME or mix, and why is specialty alloy margin (~20.5%) far above the FY31 vision?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium gains came from LME prices and product mix. Management said the 2031 ~15-17% margin is a holistic group figure and conservative, and that past targets were beaten.

qa_highlights.question: Is the softness in rebar prices seasonal or a demand weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a regular monsoon and logistics effect. Demand is expected to keep growing, and the company is focused on the annual view rather than quarterly moves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for new capacity and value-added revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium stabilises 3-4 months after commissioning, with value from Q3. Iron-making by end of Q2/early Q3, and flat products expected to more than double in FY27. Stainless run rate could reach INR600-700 crore at 70-80% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance only 20%+ growth when Q1 was up 28-30% and capacity is coming on stream?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prefers conservative guidance. It said projections are more than 25% and the numbers could be fantastic, with growth above 100% expected year on year in some parts.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise an enabling INR4,500 crore fundraising resolution if capex is internally funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is only an enabling resolution with no fundraising currently on the table. It has no major opportunity under evaluation and is prepared for future opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Emerge Green Power structure and capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: The 26% stake is a JV-style solar model, with the investee run by a PE-backed fund. Management said it avoids heavy capex, with returns around 8-10% on a buy-back model.

risks_watch: Specialty alloy and stainless margins look high versus the FY31 vision. Sustainability of CRM EBITDA at about INR8,500 per ton is uncertain given competition.
Inventory: management said it targets 2-3 months of inventory; a sizeable working capital build (around INR1,000 crore inventory cited) is exposed to commodity and geopolitical swings.
Execution risk on commissioning of aluminium foil, aluminium flat roll (Q2), iron-making (end Q2/early Q3) and power plants. Volume growth target of 25% for FY27 was not clearly confirmed.
Monsoon-quarter seasonality (Q2) could weaken volumes and realisations.
Commodity exposure: nickel is not sourced domestically for 300-series stainless, requiring imports of nickel scrap or nickel pig iron.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and margins but conservative on forward targets, repeatedly saying guidance is prudent. Evasive on specific volume numbers, the purpose of the fundraising resolution and the specialty alloy expansion, which was described as under evaluation.
key_quotes: We are very sure that, we will maintain this growth trajectory, what we had been doing in the past, and will become more and more investor and stakeholders friendly in the time to come.
We rather believe to speak less and deliver more.

We remain confident of delivering a 600 to 700 basis point improvement in return on equity and return on capital by 2031, supported by higher utilization, richer value-added product portfolio and increasing contributions from our downstream businesses.
Enabling resolution. Just -- no, it's just enabling resolution. Nothing very serious on the table.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth above 20% and EBITDA growth of 20-25%+, backed by the colour-coated plant (cold rolling capacity up 60% to 0.4 Mt, commissioned April 2026), Odisha aluminium foil commissioning, and a stainless plant ramp to INR600-700 cr quarterly revenue; the INR9,580 cr balance capex is spread over 3-4 years with no dated volume targets.
